newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- DEC 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- DEC 31.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The first Treasury bill issue of the New Year on January 2 will carry an interest rate of 11.2 percent with net interest of 10.36 percent. The government's new tax on treasury bills will be prepaid during purchase. Meanwhile, the Mortgage Bank's new bond issue will carry a net interest of 10.63 percent, higher than the state issue.

--The national economy and finance ministry has prioritised the evaluation of the state's real estate assets and will develop a policy for their best exploitation. Rents in urban centers will be speedily readjusted to market conditions while the possibility of selling real estate through the stock exchange is also being considered.
--An ICAP study has revealed that hotels had reduced returns last year but that other tourism-related sectors - car and yacht rentals, cruises - were unaffected by the fewer tourists.
--The state is seeing in the New Year with a plethora of new offers of bonds and T-bills, in an effort to cover lending needs of 1.5 trillion drachmas.

--Private Xiosbank filed with the Athens bourse for listing on its main market yesterday, the first filing in five years by a bank. Xiosbank will tap the market for over 4.0 billion drachmas and use IPO proceeds to finance its 1997-2000 investment programme.
--376 merchants and self-employed professionals were referred to the courts in November by tax officials for non-payment of Value Added Tax.

--The flow of European Union funds in December will be crucial for developments in the balance of payments and funding for Community Support Framework projects. Sources say that only 4.5 billion dollars of the promised 5.5 billion had been received by November.

--The environment, town planning and public works ministry has extended the deadline for applications to be included in the National Land Registry following a lukewarm response from landlords and owners.
--The National Bank of Greece will extend a two billion drachma loan to state-run paper mill Softex for immediate needs and until a study is conducted on the financial situation of the enterprise.

--The selection of consultants for the programme and procedures to sell a number of state-run firms will be the focus of a meeting late this week or early next, attended by the ministers of national economy and finance and development.

--National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou has given his approval for Emmanuel Xanthakis to continue as president of the Athens Stock Exchange for another three years. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
